hg-baptism.title: The Father, the Son, and the Spirit
hg-baptism.alt: Jesus looks upward beside John in the Jordan as a dove descends above Him.
hg-baptism.caption: Explore and studyThe Father, the Son, and the SpiritAt the Jordan, Matthew records the Father’s voice, the Son’s baptism, and the Spirit descending like a dove. Read the three witnesses together.Matthew 3:13-17
hg-baptism.historical_limits: Matthew records Jesus in the water, the Spirit descending like a dove, and the Father speaking. The event distinguishes their witness. The dove is a sign, not a claim that the Holy Ghost is a bird.

independent_review.scope: Actual original pixels inspected for natural anatomy, photographic appearance, story-appropriate gaze and atmosphere. Approved references used where mapped; no claim of archaeological likeness or owner aesthetic acceptance.

hg-elijah.title: A voice after the storm
hg-elijah.alt: Elijah holds his mantle over his face at the entrance to a mountain cave.
hg-elijah.caption: Explore and studyA voice after the stormAfter wind, earthquake, and fire, Elijah hears a quiet voice. He covers his face and listens at the cave entrance.1 Kings 19:9-13
hg-elijah.historical_limits: The text calls this the Lord’s voice. Use as a scriptural pattern of quiet divine communication, not proof that every OT voice is explicitly identified as the Holy Ghost.

hg-risen-commission.title: Peace and a commission

hg-pentecost.title: A witness that people can understand
hg-pentecost.alt: Visitors in Jerusalem listen with surprise as a disciple speaks to them.
hg-pentecost.caption: Explore and studyA witness that people can understandAt Pentecost, people from different places hear in languages they understand. The witness points them toward Jesus Christ.Acts 2:5-11
hg-pentecost.historical_limits: Acts records filling with the Holy Ghost, languages understood by hearers and signs. Focus on intelligible witness; do not collapse the indoor arrival and later crowd into one literal instant.
